blocks.text: יְהוָה יְהוָה אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת: נֹצֵר חֶסֶד לָאֲלָפִים נֹשֵׂא עָוֹן וָפֶשַׁע וְחַטָּאָה וְנַקֵּה:
ג״פ.

רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָם מַלֵּא מִשְׁאֲלוֹתֵינוּ לְטוֹבָה וְהָפֵק רְצוֹנֵנוּ וְתֶן־לָנוּ שְׁאֵלָתֵנוּ וּמְחֹל עַל כָּל־עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ וְעַל־כָּל־עֲוֹנוֹת אַנְשֵׁי בֵיתֵינוּ מְחִילָה בְחֶסֶד מְחִילָה בְּרַחֲמִים וְטַהֲרֵנוּ מֵחַטֹּאתֵינוּ וּמֵעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ וּמִפְּשָׁעֵינוּ. וְזָכְרֵנוּ בְּזִכְרוֹן טוֹב לְפָנֶיךָ וּפָקְדֵנוּ בִּפְקֻדַּת יְשׁוּעָה וְרַחֲמִים וְזָכְרֵנוּ לְחַיִּים אֲרֻכִּים טוֹבִים וּלְשָׁלוֹם וּפַרְנָסָה וְכַלְכָּלָה וְתֶן־לָנוּ לֶחֶם לֶאֱכֹל וּבֶגֶד לִלְבּוֹשׁ וְעֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד וְאֹרֶךְ יָמִים לַהֲגוֹת בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ וּלְקַיֵּם מִצְוֹתֶיהָ וְשֵׂכֶל וּבִינָה לְהָבִין וּלְהַשְׂכִּיל עִמְקֵי סוֹדוֹתֶיהָ וּשְׁלַח רְפוּאָה לְכָל־מַכְאוֹבֵינוּ וּתְבָרֵךְ אֶת־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ וְתִגְזֹר עָלֵינוּ גְּזֵרוֹת טוֹבוֹת יְשׁוּעוֹת וְנֶחָמוֹת וּתְבַטֵּל מֵעָלֵינוּ כָּל־גְּזֵרוֹת קָשׁוֹת. וְתַטֵּה לֵב הַמַּלְכוּת וְיוֹעֲצֶיהָ וְשָׂרֶיהָ עָלֵינוּ לְטוֹבָה. אָמֵן וְכֵן יְהִי רָצוֹן:
יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי־פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ צוּרִי וְגֹאֲלִי:
וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי־לְךָ יְיָ עֵת רָצוֹן אֱלֹהִים בְּרָב־חַסְדֶּךָ עֲנֵנִי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׁעֶךָ:
ג״פ.
Prayer while the Scrolls of the Torah are taken out of the Ark

It was when the Holy Ark set out that Moses said: Arise O Lord, that Thine enemies may be scattered and that those who hate Thee, may flee from Thy countenance. From Zion does Torah go forth and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
Blessed be He, who in His holiness gave the Torah to His people Israel.

The Lord, the Lord is a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger and great in kindness and truth; He preserves kindness to the thousandth generation, forgives guilt, transgression and sin, and purifies.

Master of the world, fulfil our wishes for the good, grant our will and give us our wish; forgive all our sins and all the sins of our household through forgiveness in grace and forgiveness in mercy and purify us from our transgressions, sins and iniquities; remember us benevolently before Thee and consider us with salvation and compassion; remember us for a long and good life, for peace, livelihood and sustenance; give us bread to eat, clothes to wear, wealth and honour, long life to ponder on Thy Torah and fulfil its commandments and sense and intelligence to grasp and understand the depths of its mysteries. Send healing for all our sufferings, bless all the work of our hands, decree for us good decrees, help and comfort; annul all harsh decrees from upon us, incline the heart of the kingdom, its advisers and princes for our good, Amen. Thus may it be Thy will.
May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart find favour before Thee, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.
My prayer goes out to Thee, O Lord, at a time of favour, O God, in Thine abundant mercy, answer me with the truth of Thy salvation.

בְּרִיךְ שְׁמֵהּ דְּמָרֵא עָלְמָא בְּרִיךְ כִּתְרָךְ וְאַתְרָךְ. יְהֵא רְעוּתָךְ עִם עַמָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעָלַם. וּפוּרְקַן יְמִינָךְ אַחֲזֵי לְעַמָּךְ בְּבֵית מִקְדְּשָׁךְ וּלְאַמְטוּיֵי לָנָא מִטּוּב נְהוֹרָךְ וּלְקַבֵּל צְלוֹתָנָא בְּרַחֲמִין. יְהֵא רַעֲוָא קֳדָמָךְ דְּתוֹרִיךְ לָן חַיִּין בְּטִיבוּתָא, וְלֶהֱוֵא אֲנָא פְקִידָא בְּגוֹ צַדִּיקַיָּא לְמִרְחַם עֲלַי וּלְמִנְטַר יָתִי וְיָת כָּל־דִּי לִי וְדִי לְעַמָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל. אַנְתְּ הוּא זָן לְכֹלָּא וּמְפַרְנֵס לְכֹלָּא. אַנְתְּ הוּא שַׁלִּיט עַל־כֹּלָּא. אַנְתְּ הוּא דְשַׁלִּיט עַל־מַלְכַיָּא וּמַלְכוּתָא דִּילָךְ הִיא. אֲנָא עַבְדָּא דְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּסָגִידְנָא קַמֵּיהּ וּמִקַּמֵּא דִּיקַר אוֹרַיְתֵהּ בְּכָל־עִדָּן וְעִדָּן. לָא עַל אֱנָשׁ רָחִיצְנָא. וְלָא עַל־בַּר־אֱלָהִין סָמִיכְנָא. אֶלָּא בֶּאֱלָהָא דִשְׁמַיָּא. דְּהוּא אֱלָהָא קְשׁוֹט. וְאוֹרַיְתֵהּ קְשׁוֹט. וּנְבִיאוֹהִי קְשׁוֹט וּמַסְגֵּא לְמֶעְבַּד טַבְוָן וּקְשׁוֹט. בֵּהּ אֲנָא רָחִיץ. וְלִשְׁמֵהּ קַדִּישָׁא יַקִּירָא אֲנָא אֵמַר תֻּשְׁבְּחָן. יְהֵא רַעֲוָא קֳדָמָךְ דְּתִפְתַּח לִבִּי בְּאוֹרַיְתָא וְתַשְׁלִים מִשְׁאֲלִין דְּלִבִּי וְלִבָּא דְכָל־עַמָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְטַב וּלְחַיִּין וְלִשְׁלָם:

גַּדְּלוּ לַייָ אִתִּי. וּנְרוֹמְמָה שְׁמוֹ יַחְדָּו:

לְךָ יְיָ הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַגְּבוּרָה וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת וְהַנֵּצַח וְהַהוֹד כִּי־כֹל בַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבָאָרֶץ לְךָ יְיָ הַמַּמְלָכָה וְהַמִּתְנַשֵּׂא לְכֹל לְרֹאשׁ: רוֹמְמוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַהֲדֹם רַגְלָיו קָדוֹשׁ הוּא: רוֹמְמוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְהַר־קָדְשׁוֹ כִּי קָדוֹשׁ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ:

עַל הַכֹּל יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאֵר וְיִתְרוֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא: שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל־מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: בָּעוֹלָמוֹת שֶׁבָּרָא הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא: כִּרְצוֹנוֹ וְכִרְצוֹן יְרֵאָיו וְכִרְצוֹן כָּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל: צוּר

Blessed be the Name of the Master of the world, blessed by Thy crown and Thy place. May Thy favour rest upon Thy people Israel in eternity. Show the salvation of Thy right hand to Thy people in Thy sanctuary, grant us the goodness of Thy light and accept our prayer with compassion; may it be Thy will to grant us a long and happy life and may I be remembered among the righteous so that Thou wilt have compassion on me and guard me and all that belongs to me and to Thy people Israel. Thou dost nourish all and sustain all; it is Thou who dost rule over all, Thou rulest over kings and the kingdom is Thine. I serve the Holy One, blessed be He, bow down before Him and His holy Torah at all times. I do not trust in men, I do not rely on angels, only on the God of heaven. He is the true God and His Torah is truth and His prophets are truth and He does goodness and truth in abundance. On Him do I rely and to His holy, honoured Name do I utter praise. Let it be Thy will to open my heart to the Torah, to grant the requests of my heart and those of the whole people of Israel for the good, for life and for peace.
Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.
Our God is One, our Lord is great, holy (and awe-inspiring) is His Name!
Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt His Name together.

Thine, O Lord, is greatness, might, glory, triumph and majesty. For all in heaven and on earth is Thine, O Lord, dominion and supremacy above all. Exalt the Lord our God, and bow down at His footstool, Holy is He. Exalt the Lord your God, and bow down before His holy mountain, for holy is the Lord our God.

Above all things let there be magnified, sanctified, praised, glorified, exalted and elevated the Name of the King of all kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, in the worlds that He created in this and the future world, according to His will and the will of those who fear Him and the will of the whole house of Israel. Rock of eternity, Lord of all creatures, God

הָעוֹלָמִים אֲדוֹן כָּל־הַבְּרִיּוֹת אֱלוֹהַּ כָּל־הַנְּפָשׁוֹת: הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּמֶרְחֲבֵי מָרוֹם הַשּׁוֹכֵן בִּשְׁמֵי שְׁמֵי קֶדֶם: קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ עַל הַחַיּוֹת וּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ עַל כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד: וּבְכֵן יִתְקַדֵּשׁ שִׁמְךָ בָּנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְעֵינֵי כָל־חָי: וְנֹאמַר לְפָנָיו שִׁיר חָדָשׁ כַּכָּתוּב: שִׁירוּ לֵאלֹהִים זַמְּרוּ שְׁמוֹ סֹלּוּ לָרֹכֵב בָּעֲרָבוֹת בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ וְעִלְזוּ לְפָנָיו: וְנִרְאֵהוּ עַיִן בְּעַיִן בְּשׁוּבוֹ אֶל נָוֵהוּ כַּכָּתוּב: כִּי עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ בְּשׁוּב יְיָ צִיּוֹן: וְנֶאֱמַר וְנִגְלָה כְבוֹד יְיָ וְרָאוּ כָל־בָּשָׂר יַחְדָּו כִּי פִּי יְיָ דִּבֵּר:

אַב הָרַחֲמִים הוּא יְרַחֵם עַם עֲמוּסִים וְיִזְכּוֹר בְּרִית אֵיתָנִים וְיַצִּיל נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ מִן הַשָּׁעוֹת הָרָעוֹת וְיִגְעַר בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע מִן הַנְּשׂוּאִים וְיָחֹן אוֹתָנוּ לִפְלֵטַת עוֹלָמִים וִימַלֵּא מִשְׁאֲלוֹתֵינוּ בְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה יְשׁוּעָה וְרַחֲמִים:

וְיַעֲזוֹר וְיָגֵן וְיוֹשִׁיעַ לְכָל הַחוֹסִים בּוֹ וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן: הַכֹּל הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ וּתְנוּ כָבוֹד לַתּוֹרָה כֹּהֵן קְרָב. יַעֲמוֹד (פלוני בר פלוני הכהן): בָּרוּךְ שֶׁנָּתַן תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדֻשָּׁתוֹ: תּוֹרַת יְיָ תְּמִימָה מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ עֵדוּת יְיָ נֶאֱמָנָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי: פִּקּוּדֵי יְיָ יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב מִצְוַת יְיָ בָּרָה מְאִירַת עֵינָיִם: יְיָ עֹז לְעַמּוֹ יִתֵּן יְיָ יְבָרֵךְ אֶת עַמּוֹ בַשָּׁלוֹם: הָאֵל תָּמִים דַּרְכּוֹ אִמְרַת יְיָ צְרוּפָה מָגֵן הוּא לְכֹל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ:
וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּייָ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם:

of all souls, who dwells in the infinite heights, and resides in the primaeval heavens, His holiness is above the Hayoth, His holiness is above the glorious throne. And thus may Thy Name be sanctified among us, O Lord our God, before the eyes of all the living; and let us sing before Him a new song, as it is written: ‘Sing to God, sing praise of His Name. Exalt Him who rides upon the clouds, Yah is His Name, and rejoice before Him. We shall see Him eye to eye when He returns to His dwelling as it is written: eye to eye shall they behold when the Lord returns to Zion. And it was said: ‘And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed and all flesh together shall see, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken’.

The father of mercy will have mercy upon the people borne by Him and remember the covenant with the eternal ones (forefathers) and deliver our souls from evil hours and rebuke the evil inclination from those whom He has lifted up and favour us for eternal refuge and fulfil our prayers with a full measure of salvation and compassion.

וַיהוָה פָּקַד אֶת־שָׂרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמָר וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוָה לְשָׂרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּר:
The Lord considered Sarah just as He had said and the Lord did for Sarah just as He had spoken.
וַתַּהַר וַתֵּלֶד שָׂרָה לְאַבְרָהָם בֵּן לִזְקֻנָיו לַמּוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּר אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים:
And Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age at the appointed time which God had told him.
וַיִּקְרָא אַבְרָהָם אֶת־שֶׁם־בְּנוֹ הַנּוֹלַד־לוֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָה־לּוֹ שָׂרָה יִצְחָק:
Abraham called the name of his son, who was born to him, whom Sarah had born to him, Isaac.
וַיָּמָל אַבְרָהָם אֶת־יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַת יָמִים כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים:
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old just as God had commanded him.
וְאַבְרָהָם בֶּן־מְאַת שָׁנָה בְּהִוָּלֶד לוֹ אֵת יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ:
Abraham was a hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born to him.
וַתֹּאמֶר שָׂרָה צְחֹק עָשָׂה לִי אֱלֹהִים כָּל־הַשֹּׁמֵעַ יִצְחַק־לִי:
Then Sarah said: ‘God has given me mirth; everyone who hears of it will laugh with me’.
וַתֹּאמֶר מִי מִלֵּל לְאַבְרָהָם הֵינִיקָה בָנִים שָׂרָה כִּי־יָלַדְתִּי בֵן לִזְקֻנָיו:
She said: ‘Who would have foretold to Abraham that Sarah would suckle children; yet have I born him a son in his old age’.
וַיִּגְדַּל הַיֶּלֶד וַיִּגָּמַל וַיַּעַשׂ אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל בְּיוֹם הִגָּמֵל אֶת־יִצְחָק:
The child grew and was weaned; and Abraham prepared a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
וַתֵּרֶא שָׂרָה אֶת־בֶּן־הָגָר הַמִּצְרִית אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָה
Then Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian
לְאַבְרָהָם מְצַחֵק:
וַתֹּאמֶר לְאַבְרָהָם גָּרֵשׁ הָאָמָה הַזֹּאת וְאֶת־בְּנָהּ כִּי לֹא יִירַשׁ בֶּן־הָאָמָה הַזֹּאת עִם־בְּנִי עִם־יִצְחָק:
וַיֵּרַע הַדָּבָר מְאֹד בְּעֵינֵי אַבְרָהָם עַל אוֹדֹת בְּנוֹ:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים אֶל־אַבְרָהָם אַל־יֵרַע בְּעֵינֶיךָ עַל־הַנַּעַר וְעַל־אֲמָתֶךָ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמַר אֵלֶיךָ שָׂרָה שְׁמַע בְּקֹלָהּ כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע:
וְגַם אֶת־בֶּן־הָאָמָה לְגוֹי אֲשִׂימֶנּוּ כִּי זַרְעֲךָ הוּא:
וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר וַיִּקַּח־לֶחֶם וְחֵמַת מַיִם וַיִּתֵּן אֶל־הָגָר שָׂם עַל־שִׁכְמָהּ וְאֶת־הַיֶּלֶד וַיְשַׁלְּחֶהָ וַתֵּלֶךְ וַתֵּתַע בְּמִדְבַּר בְּאֵר שָׁבַע:
וַיִּכְלוּ הַמַּיִם מִן־הַחֵמֶת וַתַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶת־הַיֶּלֶד תַּחַת אַחַד הַשִּׂיחִם:
וַתֵּלֶךְ וַתֵּשֶׁב לָהּ מִנֶּגֶד הַרְחֵק כִּמְטַחֲוֵי קֶשֶׁת כִּי אָמְרָה אַל־אֶרְאֶה בְּמוֹת הַיָּלֶד וַתֵּשֶׁב מִנֶּגֶד וַתִּשָּׂא אֶת־קֹלָהּ וַתֵּבְךְ:
וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־קוֹל הַנַּעַר וַיִּקְרָא מַלְאַךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶל־הָגָר מִן־הַשָּׁמַיִם וַיֹּאמֶר לָהּ מַה־לָּךְ הָגָר אַל־תִּירְאִי כִּי־שָׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶל־קוֹל הַנַּעַר בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא־שָׁם:
קוּמִי שְׂאִי אֶת־הַנַּעַר וְהַחֲזִיקִי אֶת־יָדֵךְ בּוֹ כִּי־לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל אֲשִׂימֶנּוּ:
וַיִּפְקַח אֱלֹהִים אֶת־עֵינֶיהָ וַתֵּרֶא בְּאֵר מָיִם וַתֵּלֶךְ וַתְּמַלֵּא אֶת־הַחֵמֶת מַיִם וַתַּשְׁקְ אֶת־הַנָּעַר:
וַיְהִי אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הַנַּעַר וַיִּגְדָּל וַיֵּשֶׁב בַּמִּדְבָּר וַיְהִי רֹבֶה קַשָּׁת:
וַיֵּשֶׁב בְּמִדְבַּר פָּארָן וַתִּקַּח־לוֹ אִמּוֹ אִשָּׁה מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם:
וַיְהִי בָּעֵת הַהִוא וַיֹּאמֶר אֲבִימֶלֶךְ וּפִיכֹל שַׂר־צְבָאוֹ אֶל־אַבְרָהָם לֵאמֹר אֱלֹהִים עִמְּךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּה עֹשֶׂה:
וְעַתָּה הִשָּׁבְעָה לִּי בֵאלֹהִים הֵנָּה אִם־תִּשְׁקֹר לִי וּלְנִינִי
woman, whom she had born to Abraham, scoffing.
So she said to Abraham: ‘Drive away this slave-girl and her son, for the son of this slave-girl shall not inherit together with my son, Isaac’.
And this thing seemed very wrong in Abraham’s eyes because of his son.

Then God said to Abraham: ‘Let it not seem wrong in your eyes concerning the lad and your slave-girl. With regard to all that Sarah tells you, listen to her voice, for it is through Isaac that descendants will be called after you.
And also the son of the slave-girl will I make a nation because he too is your seed’.

Then Abraham rose early in the morning and took a loaf of bread and a water-skin and gave them to Hagar, placing them upon her shoulder, as well as the child and sent her away. She went and roamed about in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water in the skin came to an end she put the child under one of the bushes.
Then she went away and sat down at a distance of a bow shot because she thought: ‘Let me not see the child die’. She sat down at a distance and raised her voice and wept.
And God heard the lad’s voice and an angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her: ‘What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid. God has heard the lad’s voice from where he is.
Rise, lift up the lad and hold him firmly with the hand, for I will make him a great nation’.
And God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water and she went and filled the skin with water and gave the lad to drink.
And God was with the lad and he grew up and lived in the wilderness and became an archer.
He lived in the wilderness of Paran and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
It was at that time that Abimelekh and Pikhol, the general of his army, spoke to Abraham saying: ‘God is with you in everything that you do.
So now swear to me here by God that you will not be untrue
וּלְנֶכְדִּי כַּחֶסֶד אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂיתִי עִמְּךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה עִמָּדִי וְעִם־הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר־גַּרְתָּה בָּהּ:
וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָהָם אָנֹכִי אִשָּׁבֵעַ:
וְהוֹכִחַ אַבְרָהָם אֶת־אֲבִימֶלֶךְ עַל־אֹדוֹת בְּאֵר הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר גָּזְלוּ עַבְדֵי אֲבִימֶלֶךְ:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֲבִימֶלֶךְ לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מִי עָשָׂה אֶת־הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה וְגַם־אַתָּה לֹא־הִגַּדְתָּ לִּי וְגַם אָנֹכִי לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי בִּלְתִּי הַיּוֹם:
וַיִּקַּח אַבְרָהָם צֹאן וּבָקָר וַיִּתֵּן לַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ וַיִּכְרְתוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּרִית:
וַיַּצֵּב אַבְרָהָם אֶת־שֶׁבַע כִּבְשֹׂת הַצֹּאן לְבַדְּהֶן:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֲבִימֶלֶךְ אֶל־אַבְרָהָם מָה הֵנָּה שֶׁבַע כְּבָשֹׂת הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר הִצַּבְתָּ לְבַדָּנָה:
וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי אֶת־שֶׁבַע כְּבָשֹׂת תִּקַּח מִיָּדִי בַּעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה־לִּי לְעֵדָה כִּי חָפַרְתִּי אֶת־הַבְּאֵר הַזֹּאת:
עַל־כֵּן קָרָא לַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא בְּאֵר שָׁבַע כִּי שָׁם נִשְׁבְּעוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם:
וַיִּכְרְתוּ בְרִית בִּבְאֵר שָׁבַע וַיָּקָם אֲבִימֶלֶךְ וּפִיכֹל שַׂר־צְבָאוֹ וַיָּשֻׁבוּ אֶל־אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים:
וַיִּטַּע אֵשֶׁל בִּבְאֵר שָׁבַע וַיִּקְרָא־שָׁם בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה אֵל עוֹלָם:
וַיָּגָר אַבְרָהָם בְּאֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים יָמִים רַבִּים:
to me or to my son or my grandson; according to the kindness that I have shown you, so may you show me kindness as well as the land in which you have resided’.
And Abraham said: ‘I swear’.
Then Abraham remonstrated with Abimelekh about the well of water which the servants of Abimelekh had stolen.
Abimelekh said: ‘I do not know who has done this; you did not tell me about it, nor have I heard about it until today’.
Then Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelekh and they both concluded a covenant.
Abraham set apart seven lambs.
Then Abimelekh said to Abraham: ‘What is the meaning of these seven lambs which you have set apart?’
He said: ‘Take these seven lambs from my hand so that these may be evidence for me that I dug this well’.
Therefore that place was called Beersheba because both of them took an oath there.
And they concluded a covenant in Beersheba. And Abimelekh arose together with Pikhol, the general of his army and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham planted a tree in Beersheba and there He called on the Name of the Lord, the God of eternity.
And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for many days.

Apart from the whole-offering of the new moon and its meal-offering and the regular whole-offering with its meal-offering and their drink-offerings according to their rule for a sweet savour, a fire offering to the Lord.

וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂם מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־פִּי יְיָ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה: עֵץ־חַיִּים הִיא לַמַּחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ וְתֹמְכֶיהָ מְאֻשָּׁר: דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי־נֹעַם וְכָל־נְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם: אֹרֶךְ יָמִים בִּימִינָהּ בִּשְׂמֹאלָהּ עֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד: יְיָ חָפֵץ לְמַעַן צִדְקוֹ יַגְדִּיל תּוֹרָה וְיַאְדִּיר:

This is the Torah which Moses placed before the Children of Israel at the Lord’s command through Moses. It is a tree of life for those who grasp it; and whoever supports it, is made happy. Its ways are pleasant and all its paths are peace. Length of days is in its right hand, in its left is wealth and honour. The Lord delights for the sake of His righteousness to magnify the Torah and to glorify it.
קודם קריאת ההפטרה ואחר שגמר הגולל, יברך המפטיר ברכה זו:
Blessing before the Haphtorah:

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר בִּנְבִיאִים טוֹבִים וְרָצָה בְדִבְרֵיהֶם הַנֶּאֱמָרִים בֶּאֱמֶת בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַבּוֹחֵר בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ וּבִנְבִיאֵי הָאֱמֶת וָצֶדֶק:

Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has chosen worthy prophets and found pleasure in their words that are spoken in truth. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who has chosen the Torah and His servant Moses, His people Israel and prophets of truth and righteousness.
הפטרה ליום א׳ של ראש השנה.
בשמואל א׳ סמן א׳.
Haphtarah

וַיְהִי אִישׁ אֶחָד מִן־הָרָמָתַיִם צוֹפִים מֵהַר אֶפְרָיִם וּשְׁמוֹ אֶלְקָנָה בֶּן־יְרֹחָם בֶּן־אֱלִיהוּא בֶּן־תֹּחוּ בֶן־צוּף אֶפְרָתִי:
וְלוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֵׁם אַחַת חַנָּה וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית פְּנִנָּה וַיְהִי לִפְנִנָּה יְלָדִים וּלְחַנָּה אֵין יְלָדִים:
וְעָלָה הָאִישׁ הַהוּא מֵעִירוֹ מִיָּמִים יָמִימָה לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֹת וְלִזְבֹּחַ לַיהוָה צְבָאוֹת בְּשִׁלֹה וְשָׁם שְׁנֵי בְנֵי־עֵלִי
חָפְנִי וּפִנְחָס כֹּהֲנִים לַיהוָה:
וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם וַיִּזְבַּח אֶלְקָנָה וְנָתַן לִפְנִנָּה אִשְׁתּוֹ וּלְכָל־בָּנֶיהָ וּבְנוֹתֶיהָ מָנוֹת:
וּלְחַנָּה יִתֵּן מָנָה אַחַת אַפָּיִם כִּי אֶת־חַנָּה אָהֵב וַיהוָה סָגַר רַחְמָהּ:
וְכִעֲסַתָּה צָרָתָהּ גַּם־כַּעַס בַּעֲבוּר הַרְּעִמָהּ כִּי־סָגַר יְהוָה בְּעַד רַחְמָהּ:
וְכֵן יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה מִדֵּי עֲלֹתָהּ בְּבֵית יְהוָה כֵּן תַּכְעִסֶנָּה וַתִּבְכֶּה וְלֹא תֹאכַל:
וַיֹּאמֶר לָהּ אֶלְקָנָה אִישָׁהּ חַנָּה לָמֶה תִבְכִּי וְלָמֶה לֹא תֹאכְלִי וְלָמֶה יֵרַע לְבָבֵךְ הֲלוֹא אָנֹכִי טוֹב לָךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָה בָּנִים:
וַתָּקָם חַנָּה אַחֲרֵי אָכְלָה בְשִׁלֹה וְאַחֲרֵי שָׁתֹה וְעֵלִי הַכֹּהֵן יֹשֵׁב עַל־הַכִּסֵּא עַל־מְזוּזַת הֵיכַל יְהוָה:
וְהִיא מָרַת נָפֶשׁ וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל עַל־יְהוָה וּבָכֹה תִבְכֶּה:

וַתִּדֹּר נֶדֶר וַתֹּאמַר יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת אִם־רָאֹה תִרְאֶה בָּעֳנִי אֲמָתֶךָ וּזְכַרְתַּנִי וְלֹא־תִשְׁכַּח אֶת־אֲמָתֶךָ וְנָתַתָּה לַאֲמָתְךָ זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים וּנְתַתִּיו לַיהוָה כָּל־יְמֵי חַיָּיו וּמוֹרָה לֹא־יַעֲלֶה עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ:
וְהָיָה כִּי הִרְבְּתָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לִפְנֵי יְהוָה וְעֵלִי שֹׁמֵר אֶת־פִּיהָ:
וְחַנָּה הִיא מְדַבֶּרֶת עַל־לִבָּהּ רַק שְׂפָתֶיהָ נָּעוֹת וְקוֹלָהּ לֹא יִשָּׁמֵעַ וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ עֵלִי לְשִׁכֹּרָה:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלֶיהָ עֵלִי עַד־מָתַי תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִין הָסִירִי
אֶת־יֵינֵךְ מֵעָלָיִךְ:
וַתַּעַן חַנָּה וַתֹּאמֶר לֹא אֲדֹנִי אִשָּׁה קְשַׁת־רוּחַ אָנֹכִי וְיַיִן וְשֵׁכָר לֹא שָׁתִיתִי וָאֶשְׁפֹּךְ אֶת־נַפְשִׁי לִפְנֵי יְהוָה:
אַל־תִּתֵּן אֶת־אֲמָתְךָ לִפְנֵי בַּת־בְּלִיָּעַל כִּי־מֵרֹב שִׂיחִי וְכַעְסִי דִּבַּרְתִּי עַד־הֵנָּה:
וַיַּעַן עֵלִי וַיֹּאמֶר לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם וֵאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יִתֵּן אֶת־שֵׁלָתֵךְ אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתְּ מֵעִמּוֹ:
וַתֹּאמֶר תִּמְצָא שִׁפְחָתְךָ חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ וַתֵּלֶךְ הָאִשָּׁה לְדַרְכָּהּ וַתֹּאכַל וּפָנֶיהָ לֹא־הָיוּ־לָהּ עוֹד:
וַיַּשְׁכִּמוּ בַבֹּקֶר וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לִפְנֵי יְהוָה וַיָּשֻׁבוּ וַיָּבֹאוּ אֶל־בֵּיתָם הָרָמָתָה וַיֵּדַע אֶלְקָנָה אֶת־חַנָּה אִשְׁתּוֹ וַיִּזְכְּרֶהָ יְהוָה:
וַיְהִי לִתְקֻפוֹת הַיָּמִים וַתַּהַר חַנָּה וַתֵּלֶד בֵּן וַתִּקְרָא אֶת־שְׁמוֹ שְׁמוּאֵל כִּי מֵיְהוָה שְׁאִלְתִּיו:
וַיַּעַל הָאִישׁ אֶלְקָנָה וְכָל־בֵּיתוֹ לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהוָה אֶת־זֶבַח הַיָּמִים וְאֶת־נִדְרוֹ:
וְחַנָּה לֹא עָלָתָה כִּי־אָמְרָה לְאִישָׁהּ עַד יִגָּמֵל הַנַּעַר וַהֲבִאֹתִיו וְנִרְאָה אֶת־פְּנֵי יְהוָה וְיָשַׁב שָׁם עַד־עוֹלָם:
וַיֹּאמֶר לָהּ אֶלְקָנָה אִישָׁהּ עֲשִׂי הַטּוֹב בְּעֵינַיִךְ שְׁבִי עַד־גָּמְלֵךְ אֹתוֹ אַךְ יָקֵם יְהוָה אֶת־דְּבָרוֹ וַתֵּשֶׁב הָאִשָּׁה וַתֵּינֶק אֶת־בְּנָהּ עַד־גָּמְלָהּ אֹתוֹ:
וַתַּעֲלֵהוּ עִמָּהּ כַּאֲשֶׁר גְּמָלַתּוּ בְּפָרִים שְׁלֹשָׁה וְאֵיפָה אַחַת קֶמַח וְנֵבֶל יַיִן וַתְּבִאֵהוּ בֵית־יְהוָה
שִׁלוֹ וְהַנַּעַר נָעַר:
וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ אֶת־הַפָּר וַיָּבִיאוּ אֶת־הַנַּעַר אֶל־עֵלִי:
וַתֹּאמֶר בִּי אֲדֹנִי חֵי נַפְשְׁךָ אֲדֹנִי אֲנִי הָאִשָּׁה הַנִּצֶּבֶת עִמְּכָה בָּזֶה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶל־יְהוָה:
אֶל־הַנַּעַר הַזֶּה הִתְפַּלָּלְתִּי וַיִּתֵּן יְהוָה לִי אֶת־שְׁאֵלָתִי אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתִּי מֵעִמּוֹ:
וְגַם אָנֹכִי הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ לַיהוָה כָּל־הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר הָיָה הוּא שָׁאוּל לַיהוָה וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ שָׁם לַיהוָה:
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל חַנָּה וַתֹּאמַר עָלַץ לִבִּי בַּיהוָה רָמָה קַרְנִי בַּיהוָה רָחַב פִּי עַל־אוֹיְבַי כִּי שָׂמַחְתִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ:
אֵין־קָדוֹשׁ כַּיהוָה כִּי אֵין בִּלְתֶּךָ וְאֵין צוּר כֵּאלֹהֵינוּ:
אַל־תַּרְבּוּ תְדַבְּרוּ גְּבֹהָה גְבֹהָה יֵצֵא עָתָק מִפִּיכֶם כִּי אֵל דֵּעוֹת יְהוָה וְלֹא נִתְכְּנוּ עֲלִלוֹת:
קֶשֶׁת גִּבֹּרִים חַתִּים וְנִכְשָׁלִים אָזְרוּ חָיִל:
שְׂבֵעִים בַּלֶּחֶם נִשְׂכָּרוּ וּרְעֵבִים חָדֵלּוּ עַד־עֲקָרָה יָלְדָה שִׁבְעָה וְרַבַּת בָּנִים אֻמְלָלָה:
יְהוָה מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה מוֹרִיד שְׁאוֹל וַיָּעַל:
יְהוָה מוֹרִישׁ וּמַעֲשִׁיר מַשְׁפִּיל אַף־מְרוֹמֵם:
מֵקִים מֵעָפָר דָּל מֵאַשְׁפֹּת יָרִים אֶבְיוֹן לְהוֹשִׁיב עִם־נְדִיבִים וְכִסֵּא כָבוֹד יַנְחִלֵם כִּי לַיהוָה מְצֻקֵי אֶרֶץ וַיָּשֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶם תֵּבֵל:
רַגְלֵי חֲסִידוֹ יִשְׁמֹר וּרְשָׁעִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ יִדָּמּוּ כִּי־לֹא בְכֹחַ יִגְבַּר־אִישׁ:
יְהוָה יֵחַתּוּ
מְרִיבָיו עָלָיו בַּשָּׁמַיִם יַרְעֵם יְהוָה יָדִין אַפְסֵי־אָרֶץ וְיִתֶּן־עֹז לְמַלְכּוֹ וְיָרֵם קֶרֶן מְשִׁיחוֹ:

blocks.text: There was once a man from Romathaim-Tsofim, from the hill-country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah the son of Yeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Tsuf, an Efrathite.
He had two wives; the name of one was Hannah and that of the other was Peninah; Peninah had children but Hannah had no children.
This man used to go up from his town year by year to Shiloh in order to prostrate himself and to sacrifice before the Lord of Hosts. There were two sons of Eli, Hofni and Pinhas, priests to the Lord.
On
the day that Elkanah sacrificed, he used to give portions to his wife Peninah and to all her sons and daughters
but to Hannah he used to give a double portion because he loved Hannah even though the Lord had closed her womb.
Her rival used to annoy her by taunting her that the Lord had closed her womb.
He used to do this year by year and whenever she went up to the house of the Lord, her rival would annoy her so that she used to weep and would not eat.
Once her husband Elkanah said to her: ‘Hannah, why do you weep, why do you not eat and why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten children?’
Hannah arose after eating and drinking in Shiloh: and Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the Sanctuary of the Lord
when she in bitterness of soul prayed to the Lord and was weeping violently.

And she made a vow and said: ‘O Lord of Hosts, if Thou wilt only look at the misery of Thy handmaid and remember me and not forget Thy handmaid and give Thy handmaid a male child, I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life and no razor shall come upon his head’.
And it happened when she prayed so much before the Lord that Eli noticed her mouth.
For Hannah was talking to herself, only her lips were moving but her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought that she was drunk
and Eli said to her: ‘How much longer will you be drunk?
Remove your wine from yourself’.
Then Hannah answered saying: ‘It is not so, my lord; I am a woman with a heavy heart, I have drunk neither wine nor mead but I have poured out my soul before the Lord.
Do not consider your handmaid as a worthless woman for it is owing to the abundance of my grief and distress that I have spoken so long’.
Eli replied and said: ‘Go forth in peace and the God of Israel will grant your request which you asked of Him’.
She said: ‘May your handmaid find favour in your eyes’. Then the woman went her way, she ate and her face was no longer sad.
They rose early in the morning and prostrated themselves before the Lord, then they returned and arrived at their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew his wife Hannah and the Lord remembered her;
and in the course of time Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She called his name Samuel ‘for I have asked for him of the Lord’.
And the man Elkanah and the whole of his household went up to offer the annual sacrifice and his vow to the Lord.
Hannah, however, did not go up, for she said to her husband: ‘When the lad has been weaned, then I will bring him there that he may appear before the presence of the Lord and stay there for ever’.
Her husband Elkanah said to her: ‘Do what is best in your eyes, stay until you have weaned him; surely the Lord will fulfil His word’. The woman stayed and suckled her son until she had weaned him.
Then she brought him up with her after she had weaned him, together with three bullocks, one ephah of flour and one bottle of wine. She brought him into the House of the Lord
at Shiloh. The lad was still very young.
They slaughtered the bullock, and brought the lad to Eli.
She said: ‘I pray you, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here to pray to the Lord.
For this lad did I pray and the Lord granted my request for which I asked of Him.
I then dedicated him to the Lord; all the days that he exists, he is dedicated to the Lord’. Then he bowed down there before the Lord.
And Hannah prayed and said: ‘My heart has rejoiced in the Lord, my condition has been raised through the Lord; my mouth has triumphed over my enemies since I have rejoiced in Thy salvation.
None is holy as the Lord for there is none besides Thee and there is no rock like our God.
Do not continue to talk haughtily, let insolence leave your mouth for a God of knowledge is the Lord and to Him all deeds are known.
The bow of the mighty breaks and stumblers are girded with strength,
those once satisfied with food hire themselves out and the hungry cease to be hungry, even she who was childless has given birth to seven while another rich in children is forlorn.
The Lord slays and revives, brings down to the grave and raises up.
The Lord impoverishes and enriches, brings low and raises high,

lifting the poor from the dust and the needy from the dung-heap to seat them with nobles and endow them with a glorious throne, for the earth’s foundations are the Lord’s and He has placed the world upon them.
He guards the feet of his pious ones but evil doers are silenced in darkness for it is not by might that
man prevails.
As for the Lord, His opponents will be crushed, in heaven above does He thunder, the Lord will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to His king and raise the condition of his anointed.
המפטיר יברך ברכות האחרונות.
Blessings after the Haphtorah:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם צוּר כָּל־הָעוֹלָמִים צַדִּיק בְּכָל־הַדּוֹרוֹת הָאֵל הַנֶּאֱמָן הָאוֹמֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה הַמְדַבֵּר וּמְקַיֵּם שֶׁכָּל־דְּבָרָיו אֱמֶת וָצֶדֶק:
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, Rock of all eternity, just in all generations, faithful God who says and acts, speaks and fulfils, for all His words are truth and righteousness.

נֶאֱמָן אַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְנֶאֱמָנִים דְּבָרֶיךָ וְדָבָר אֶחָד מִדְּבָרֶיךָ אָחוֹר לֹא־יָשׁוּב רֵיקָם כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ נֶאֱמָן וְרַחֲמָן אַתָּה. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הָאֵל הַנֶּאֱמָן בְּכָל־דְּבָרָיו:

Faithful art Thou, O Lord our God and faithful are Thy words and not one of Thy words turns back empty; for Thou art a faithful and compassionate God and King. Blessed art Thou, O Lord God who is faithful in all His words.
רַחֵם עַל־צִיּוֹן כִּי הִיא בֵּית חַיֵּינוּ וְלַעֲלוּבַת נֶפֶשׁ תּוֹשִׁיעַ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מְשַׂמֵּחַ צִיּוֹן בְּבָנֶיהָ:
Have mercy upon Zion, it is the centre of our life; and save her, whose soul is afflicted, speedily in our days. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who makes Zion rejoice with her children.

שַׂמְּחֵנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא עַבְדֶּךָ וּבְמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מְשִׁיחֶךָ בִּמְהֵרָה יָבֹא וְיָגֵל לִבֵּנוּ. עַל־כִּסְאוֹ לֹא־יֵשֵׁב זָר וְלֹא יִנְחֲלוּ עוֹד אֲחֵרִים אֶת־כְּבוֹדוֹ. כִּי בְשֵׁם קָדְשְׁךָ נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ לּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא־יִכְבֶּה נֵרוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מָגֵן דָּוִד:

Let us rejoice, O Lord our God, with the prophet Elijah Thy servant and with the realm of the House of David thine anointed. Speedily may he come that our heart may have joy. Let no stranger sit on his throne, and let others no longer inherit his glory for by Thy Holy Name hast Thou sworn to him that his light shall not be extinguished for ever. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, shield of David.

עַל הַתּוֹרָה וְעַל־הָעֲבוֹדָה וְעַל־הַנְּבִיאִים וְעַל־יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְיוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה שֶׁנָּתַתָּ לָּנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ (לִקְדֻשָּׁה וְלִמְנוּחָה) לְכָבוֹד וּלְתִפְאָרֶת. עַל־הַכֹּל יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ וּמְבָרְכִים אוֹתָךְ. יִתְבָּרַךְ שִׁמְךָ בְּפִי־כָל־חַי תָּמִיד לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. וּדְבָרְךָ אֱמֶת וְקַיָּם לָעַד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ מְקַדֵּשׁ (הַשַּׁבָּת וְ) יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן:

For the Torah, for the service of God, for the prophets and for this (Sabbath day and this) day of memorial, which Thou, O Lord our God, hast given us, (for holiness and rest) for honour and glory, for all these, O Lord our God, do we thank Thee and bless Thee. Blessed be Thy name in the mouth of all the living constantly and for ever and ever, Thy word is truth and endures to eternity. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, King over all the earth who sanctifies (the Sabbath) Israel and the day of memorial.
